openItems.topic: Measurement device conditions and support baseline
openItems.known: Four devices report webview rendering, callable wx.getPerformance, registered observers and the same six runtime-supported types. After the snapshot-source correction was requested, OPPO returned 10 rows, down from 20; the previous visible repeated type/duration patterns are absent. Six rows display durations (appLaunch 1532ms, firstRender 701ms, evaluateScript 4ms, plus redacted render/interaction values); route and the three paint/content timing points have no duration. The OPPO report does not embed its probe revision. A new SEA-AL10 report shows WeChat 8.0.79/base library 3.17.5 (earlier report was 3.17.4); the user confirmed Android GPU Rendering bars appeared over the WeChat probe and refreshed while scrolling. ADB confirms the connected device is SEA-AL10/Android 10/API 29 and foreground AppBrandUI00 during capture. SurfaceFlinger returned an attributable host layer but its first capture spanned about 33 seconds and was not synchronized to scrolling. A separate read-only gfxinfo query against com.tencent.mm:appbrand0 returned a ViewRoot matching AppBrandUI00; the main WeChat process was excluded because its ViewRoot was LauncherUI. Before reset, the process showed 3033 cumulative frames and 13 janky frames. The first reset exited 0 and its stats-since timestamp changed; a post-reset query restarted at 66 frames. A later unsynchronized read showed 301 frames/0 janky. A second reset before the requested gesture changed the stats-since timestamp and verified zero frames immediately afterward. The first post-scroll dump showed 1636 aggregate frames/0 janky across about 240.6 seconds and no input timestamps. A later 15.226-second live poll overlapped a user-confirmed approximate five-second scroll: the count stayed at 0 through 5.331 seconds, then rose to 203 frames with 1 janky frame (0.49%). The gesture start/end were not logged, and all ten final rows had NewestInputEvent=0 and the no-event OldestInputEvent sentinel. A later guarded synthetic swipe on the visible AppBrandUI00 host returned 93 frames/0 janky over 5.419 seconds of host command time, but its ten recent rows had no input timestamps and the WebView compositor was not isolated. This is feasibility data only, not a scroll FPS or QP05 result. No frame-rate item was found in the IDE Tools menu; System Tracing was not found under Debugging on the backup Huawei.

openItems.localTraceEvidence: A seven-second atrace overlapped a five-second synthetic swipe and retained 61,017/61,017 events. Input, AppBrand doFrame and SurfaceFlinger vsync markers were present, but no separately attributable WebView presented-frame stream was found. Perfetto's traced service disconnected and a larger atrace buffer failed; a 1,024 KB buffer succeeded. This is measurement-method feasibility only.
openItems.oppoFrameTimelineEvidence: PLJ110 / Android 17 exposed an AppBrandUI00 actual-frame layer. At 120Hz an earlier trace recorded 84 host frames over 1.010 seconds. At confirmed active 60Hz, the first short trace captured input but no host frames; after moving the diagnostic page toward the top, a second trace captured 152 host frames over 2.845 seconds with 1,204 input-delivery slices. The WebView layer and full gesture remain unisolated, 948 systrace import errors remain, and the 329.57ms adjacent host-frame gap cannot be attributed to an app stall. Method feasibility only, not QP05 evidence.
openItems.nextAction: Keep R03 pending. Verify whether the AppBrand FrameTimeline host layer represents the actual mini-program product page without unrelated frame sources. Freeze a 60Hz measurement device, supported sampler, 200-item heavy-content page and input segment length before collecting QP05's repeated runs. Do not calculate FPS from the diagnostic page's one-second frame burst. Determine the iPhone sampling path, rerun the latest isolated probe on the other phones, and resolve the route-duration question.

openItems.known: Home Wi-Fi and public free Wi-Fi are user-confirmed scenes. An authorized OPPO/home-Wi-Fi run of the existing read-only identity endpoint returned 30/30 successful application round trips; recomputed P50=284ms, P95=470ms, max=1701ms. Two separate Cloudflare speed-test screenshots reported down 25.5/27.1 Mbps, up 33.5/25.1 Mbps, latency 200/191ms, jitter 40/74.3ms and packet loss 14.3/1.8%; the user confirmed the same OPPO/home Wi-Fi, while the screenshots do not independently verify device/access. The Cloudflare target differs from CloudBase. The user has borrowed a China Telecom-customized Zhaonengxuntong ZN-M2 router; firmware and owner permission for isolated configuration are unknown. On 2026-11-01 the user said the router owner is temporarily unavailable to ask, so no firmware, management-access or configuration-consent evidence is available. A third-party firmware project does not prove this device runs OpenWrt. The large packet-loss variation prevents freezing a stable normal network profile.
